### 2026-10-11 – I noticed in the starbie guide repo, a new commit was made to switch the SDA and SCL pins  in firmware, so I checked my PCB and lo and behold the pins were assigned the wrong way round in the schemati

**7h**

I noticed in the starbie guide repo, a new commit was made to switch the SDA and SCL pins  in firmware, so I checked my PCB and lo and behold the pins were assigned the wrong way round in the schematic attached to the esp32, so I switched them round. This also means that I had to reroute that section of the board, which was much more difficult this time since the lines had to cross over each other, so I solved this by using some vias (as seen in the image below).

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/fvXf9yz5DFN3iRWyOJOL0QEAq4gD0FtX/5559e99da0f7bd095c70a39b4f54e14cbeae8e50974544be8115be67023c2e0e.png)

I also used this opportunity to regenerate the gerbers and upload them to JLCPCB for a quote on the pcb cost and delivery, which I used to update the BOM.

![Screenshot 2026-10-11 182627](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/fvXf9yz5DFN3iRWyOJOL0QEAq4gD0FtX/b10e51cf40243d01da3573f01ac4518420d20e92ff45f4384d9bc4ea6a3f3c6a.png)

After this I went to find the rest of the parts required for the project. There was a BOM attached to the guide project, so first I tried to use the parts listed there (they have links for amazon), but the cost was much more than stated on the aforementioned and would not fit within the budget. Since I couldn't use the supplied links, I searched about and finally landed on a list of parts from alibaba which did fit within the budget (including shipping).

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/fvXf9yz5DFN3iRWyOJOL0QEAq4gD0FtX/fa2aa26a9edc72ed4e33827f4d6d362ba7cad0cee3b7f51b380d1eab27b2fb4a.png)

It should be noted that when designing the PCB, I used the MX switch footprint provided by the guide, but when choosing the switch, I ended up going for this gateron switch which, according to information online and this product photo, uses the same footprint and should still work in the pcb.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/fvXf9yz5DFN3iRWyOJOL0QEAq4gD0FtX/645da88c6605e318b3761d8bb01559e4bf4985763a3343811cb8c3f0f77065c7.png)

Once this was done,  the last thing to do was write the firmware. I decided that since I am more comfortable with the software side of this project, I would not just use the firmware from the guide. Instead, I read through the code and designed my own firmware (using the same libraries) which, instead of showing a virtual pet, simply shows the output of all of the sensors and buttons on one screen.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/fvXf9yz5DFN3iRWyOJOL0QEAq4gD0FtX/9e4cc87d695c49ff1ec81022d280c176c0402f917b1fbcf22267b27c51302247.png)

This firmware is simpler but can be upgraded at a later point with additional functionality. I have drawn two mockups showing an example state that could be displayed on the screen below.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/fvXf9yz5DFN3iRWyOJOL0QEAq4gD0FtX/f30bbbb3b5ccbbacb9ab69d9bcd678a51a04d4178409de4ffe04a81a7013563b.png)

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/hackclub-half-life/sessions/fvXf9yz5DFN3iRWyOJOL0QEAq4gD0FtX/09417d3e19cca40f13784709e4ab6d03c8d433225c9d97f06063b826120e7ec8.png)

The circle in the center uses the gyro and accelerometer to determine the orientation of the device, and displays it with the smaller filled circle indicating the current tilt.
